questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two containers ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ of volumes $V$ and $4V$ respectively, hold the same ideal gas and are connected by a thin horizontal tube of negligible volume with a valve which is initially closed. The initial pressures of the gas in ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ are $p$ and $5p$, respectively. Heat baths are employed to maintain the temperatures in the containers at $300K$ and $400K$, respectively. The valve is now opened. Select the correct statement.
options: The gas will flow from the hot container to the cold one and the process is reversible.
The gas will flow from one container to the other till the number of moles in two containers are equal.
A long time after the valve is opened, the pressure in both the containers will be $3p$.
A long time after the valve is opened, number of moles of gas in the hot container will be thrice that of the cold one.
questions.solution:
Let ${n}_{1}$ and ${n}_{2}$ are number of moles of gas present in container ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ respectively, before the value is opened.

Then, using $pV = nRT$.

${n}_{1} = \dfrac{pV}{R\left(300\right)}$

and ${n}_{2} = \dfrac{5p\left(4V\right)}{R\left(400\right)}$

When value is opened gas flows from ${C}_{2}$ to ${C}_{1}$ till pressure in ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ is equal. Let after equalisation of pressure in both ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$, its value is ${p}_{0}$,

Then, using $pV = nRT$.

${p}_{0}V = {n}_{1}^{'}R\left(300\right)$ (Container ${C}_{1}$)

and ${p}_{0}4V = {n}_{2}^{'}R\left(400\right)$ (Container ${C}_{2}$)

So, ${n}_{1}^{'} = \dfrac{{p}_{0}V}{R\left(300\right)}$

As no gas is leaked from containers, 

${n}_{1} + {n}_{2} = {n}_{1}^{'}: {n}_{2}^{'}$

$⇒ \dfrac{pV}{R\left(300\right)} + \dfrac{20pV}{R\left(400\right)}$

$= \dfrac{{p}_{0}V}{R\left(300\right)} + \dfrac{4{p}_{0}V}{R\left(400\right)}$

So, $p\left(\dfrac{1}{300} + \dfrac{20}{400}\right) = {p}_{0}\left(\dfrac{1}{300} + \dfrac{4}{400}\right)$

$⇒ 4p = {p}_{0}$

Now, ${n}_{2}^{'}{n}_{1}^{'} = \dfrac{\dfrac{4{p}_{0}V}{R\left(400\right)}}{\dfrac{{p}_{0}V}{R\left(300\right)}} = 3$

Finally number of moles of ${C}_{2}$ is thrice of ${C}_{1}$.

Work done by monoatomic gas is more than that by diatomic gas
Work done by both the gases are equal
Change in internal energies of both the gases are equal

Expansion curves are as shown below.

As, slope of an adiabatic curve $= - \gamma \left(\dfrac{p}{V}\right)

Also, ${γ}_{diatomic} $\left(= \dfrac{7}{5}\right) < {γ}_{monoatomic}\left(= \dfrac{5}{3}\right)$

As, work done $=$ area under $p - V$ graph

questions.q: A thermally insulated rigid container of $1L$ volume contains a diatomic ideal gas at room temperature. A small paddle installed inside the container is rotated from the outside, such that the pressure rises by ${10}^{5}Pa$. The change in internal energy is close to
questions.solution:
Change in internal energy of $n$ moles of an ideal gas, when temperature changes by $\Delta T$ is

$\Delta U = n \cdot \dfrac{f}{2} \cdot R \cdot \Delta T$

$= \dfrac{f}{2} \lleft(nR\Delta T\right) = \dfrac{f}{2} \left(\Deltap \cdotV\right)$

[$∴$ for ideal gas $pV = nRT$]

Here, $f = 5$ (gas is diatomic)

$\Deltap = {10}^{5}Pa, V = 1L = {10}^{- 3}m^{3}$

So, $\Delta U = \dfrac{5}{2} \times {10}^{5} \times {10}^{- 3} =250J$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For an ideal gas, the internal energy is given by $U = 5pV / 2 + C,$ where $C$ is a constant. The equation of the adiabats in the $pV$-plane will be
questions.solution:
For an ideal gas,

${C}_{V} = {\dfrac{∂ U}{∂ T}}_{V = constant}$

or ${C}_{V} = \dfrac{dU}{dT}$

Also, for $1$~mole of gas,

${C}_{V} = \dfrac{f}{2} \cdot R$

where, $f =$~degree of freedom. Hence, we have

$\dfrac{f}{2}R = \dfrac{dU}{dT}$

Here, $U = \dfrac{5}{2}pV + C = \dfrac{5}{2}RT + C$

[$∵$ one mole of gas is considered]

So, $\dfrac{f}{2}R = \dfrac{d}{dT} $\$left(\dfrac{5}{2}$RT + C\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{f}{2}$R = $\dfrac{5}{2}$R ⇒ f = 5$

Now, using $\gamma =1 + $\dfrac{2}{f}$$

where, $\gamma =$ratio of specific heats~$=$ adiabatic index.

We have, $\gamma =1 + $\dfrac{2}{5}$⇒ \gamma = $\dfrac{7}{5}$$

So, equation of adiabats can be written as $pV^{γ} =$ constant $⇒ pV^{7 / 5} =$ constant

$⇒ p^{5}V^{7} =$ constant

questions.q: Graphs below show the entropy versus energy $U$ of two systems $1$ and $2$ at constant volume. The initial energies of the systems are indicated by ${U}_{1, i}$ and ${U}_{2, i},$ respectively. Graphs are drawn to the same scale. The systems are then brought into thermal contact with each other. Assume that, at all times the combined energy of the two systems remains constant. Choose the most appropriate option indicating the energies of the two systems and the total entropy after they achieve the equilibrium.
options: ${U}_{1}$ increases and ${U}_{2}$ decreases and the total entropy remains the same
${U}_{1}$ decreases and ${U}_{2}$ increases and the total entropy remains the same
${U}_{1}$ increases and ${U}_{2}$ decreases and the total entropy increases
${U}_{1}$ decreases and ${U}_{2}$ increases and the total entropy increases
questions.solution:
By second law of thermodynamics, entropy of a system either increases or remains constant (only in reversible quasistatic processes).

Also, from graphs given
${S}_{2} > {S}_{1} ⇒ \dfrac{Q}{T2} > \dfrac{Q}{T1}$

where, $S$ is entropy, $Q$ is heat and $T$ is the temperature.
or ${T}_{1} < {T}_{2}$

Hence, temperature of system $1$ is less than system $2.$ So, heat flows from system $2$ to system $1$.

Hence, ${U}_{1}$ increases and ${U}_{2}$ decreases.

questions.solution:
Process equation is $pV^{2} = \beta... ( i )$

As gas is ideal, it obeys gas equation, $pV = nRT... ( iii )$

From Eqs. $( i )$ and $( ii )$, gives

$( nRT ) \cdot V = \beta$

Here, $n = 0. 02$ moles,

$R = 8. 31{JK}^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}, T = 20 ° C + 273 = 293K$

and $V = 1500{cm}^{3} = 1. 5 \times {10}^{- 3}m^{3}$

$∴ \beta = 0. 02 \times 8. 31 \times 293 \times 1. 5 \times {10}^{- 3}$

$= 7. 3 \times {10}^{- 2}Pa - m^{6}$

$\approx 7. 5 \times {10}^{- 2}Pa - m^{6}$

&

& Hot air balloon will rise in the atmosphere when upthrust of buoyant force is greater than weight of balloon and its payload. Upthrust = Weight of atmospheric air displaced by balloon So, upthrust ≥ weight of balloon and its payload
$⇒$ (Volume of air displaced $\times$ density of atmospheric air $\times$ Acceleration due to gravity) ≥ (Volume of air of inside balloon
x density of air inside balloon $\times$ acceleration due to gravity) + (Weight of payload of balloon) $⇒ V \cdot {ρ}_{o} \cdot g \ge V \cdot {ρ}_{i} \cdot g + 210 \times g$

where ${ρ}_{o} =$ density of outside air and ${ρ}_{i} =$ density of inside air.

$⇒ V\left({ρ}_{o} - {ρ}_{i}\right) = 210⇒ {ρ}_{0} - {ρ}_{i} = \dfrac{210 \times 3}{4\pir^{3}}\left(∵ V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}\right)⇒ \dfrac{PM}{R{T}_{0}} - \dfrac{PM}{R{T}_{i}} = \dfrac{210 \times 3}{4 \times \pi \times \left(\dfrac{11.7}{2}\right)^{3}} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{T0} - \dfrac{1}{Ti}= \dfrac{680 \times 8 \times 8.31}{4 \times \pi \times ( 11.7 {)}^{3} \times {10}^{5} \times 30 \times {10}^{- 3}}⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{i} - {T}_{0}}{{T}_{0}{T}_{i}} = \dfrac{1}{1387}$

$⇒ {T}_{0}{T}_{i} = 1387\left({T}_{i} - {T}_{o}\right)⇒ 300{T}_{i} = 1387{T}_{i} - 300 \times 1387\begin{array}{ll}\text{(as,}\left{T}_{0} = {27}^{∘}C = 300K\right)\end{array}\text{So,}{T}_{i} = \dfrac{300 \times 1387}{1087} \approx 383K∴ {T}_{i} = 383 - 273 = {110}^{∘}C$

So, temperature of hot air is near to $105 ° C$.
